title: Confidentiality and Privilege Leakage Testing for Legal AI
summary: Test your legal copilot, contract tool or client chatbot for cross-matter leakage, privilege exposure, prompt injection hidden in documents and weak access controls, with evidence and fixes.

seo.title: Confidentiality Testing for Legal AI Tools | VipraTech
seo.description: Security testing of legal AI copilots and chatbots for cross-matter data leakage, privilege exposure, ethical wall bypass and document prompt injection.

problem.intro: Firms and legal departments are connecting AI copilots to document management systems, matter workspaces and data rooms. The features that make them useful, retrieval across documents and memory of past work, can expose one client's information to another matter team, reveal privileged advice, or follow instructions a counterparty has planted inside a document.

pain_points.title: Ethical walls not enforced
pain_points.detail: Retrieval layers sometimes index content without carrying over matter permissions, so a user can see material from a walled-off matter.

pain_points.title: Instructions hidden in documents
pain_points.detail: A counterparty draft or data room file can contain text that tells the AI to downplay a risk or reveal other content.

pain_points.title: Privileged content in logs and vendors
pain_points.detail: Prompts, outputs and telemetry may store privileged material with a vendor or in logs that wider teams can read.

pain_points.title: Client chatbots oversharing
pain_points.detail: A client-facing assistant can be coaxed into revealing other clients' names, fees or internal guidance.

solution.overview: We run a confidentiality-focused security assessment of your legal AI tool. With your team we map matters, permissions and data flows, then seed canary documents into restricted test matters. Testers act as users on other matters and as external clients, trying direct questions, multi-turn social engineering, system-prompt extraction and indirect prompt injection through uploaded contracts, emails and data room files. We check whether retrieval honours matter permissions, what prompts and outputs are stored and where, and whether agent tools such as email or document export can be misused. Findings come with evidence, severity, mapping to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and fixes, followed by a re-test.
capabilities: Ethical wall testing with canary documents in restricted test matters
Indirect prompt injection through contracts, emails and data room files
Client-chatbot tests for disclosure of other clients' information and internal guidance
Review of logging, telemetry and vendor retention of prompts and outputs
Tool-use abuse tests for email, export and document-sharing actions

workflow.title: Map matters and data flows
workflow.detail: We document matter permissions, connected repositories, vendors, logs and the tools the AI can use.

workflow.title: Seed canaries
workflow.detail: Unique canary documents are placed in restricted test matters with your IT team's approval.

workflow.title: Run attacks
workflow.detail: Testers attempt cross-matter retrieval, injection through documents, prompt extraction and tool misuse.

workflow.title: Check leakage paths
workflow.detail: Logs, telemetry and vendor settings are inspected for retained privileged or client content.

workflow.title: Confirm findings
workflow.detail: Each suspected leak is reproduced and reviewed with your security lead.

workflow.title: Report and re-test
workflow.detail: You receive evidence, severity and fixes, and we re-test after remediation.

inputs: Staging or controlled production access to the AI tool
Matter and permission structure, including ethical walls
List of connected repositories, vendors and tools
Test accounts across matters and roles
Rules of engagement agreed with IT and risk
outputs: Findings with reproduction steps and evidence
Mapping to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and NIST AI RMF
Review of data retention and logging
human_in_the_loop: Your security lead and our tester confirm each finding together before it is reported, and your risk and IT leadership decide on remediation and go-live. No real client documents are used as test material.
integrations: Legal AI copilot or chatbot under test
Document management system such as iManage, NetDocuments or SharePoint
Identity provider and matter permission system
guardrails: Only synthetic canary documents and test matters are used
Testing follows written rules of engagement and agreed time windows
Findings and evidence shared only with named contacts
Any real client data seen during testing is reported and not retained
Re-tests reuse the same scenarios so results are comparable
compliance_notes: Helps you evidence the confidentiality safeguards expected under Bar Council of India rules and the protection of privilege under Indian evidence law.
Supports DPDP Act 2023 security safeguard obligations and, for EU data, GDPR security requirements.

pilot.scope: One AI tool connected to one document repository, tested across a small set of restricted test matters and user roles.
deliverables: Findings report with evidence and fixes

what_we_measure.how: Count of reproduced findings by category and severity.
Canary documents retrieved or quoted to users without matter access.
Planted document instructions that changed the tool's behaviour.
Findings that no longer reproduce on re-test.

faqs.q: Do you need access to real client files?
faqs.a: No. We use synthetic canary documents in test matters. If testers see real client data by accident, it is reported immediately and not retained.

faqs.q: Can you test a vendor's legal AI product we have licensed?
faqs.a: Yes, within your licence terms and with the vendor's agreement where required. Many of the most important tests concern how the tool is connected to your systems and permissions.

It is text inside a document, email or web page that the AI reads and treats as an instruction, such as a hidden line telling it to describe a contract as low risk. Legal tools read counterparty documents constantly, so we test this specifically.
Before launch, after major changes to models, prompts, connected repositories or permissions, and periodically after that. The test suite can be re-run to compare results over time.
